hook: Terence Tao is a mathematician whose work spans harmonic analysis, partial differential equations, number theory and combinatorics, and who has more recently turned his attention to using computers and formal proof systems to assist mathematical research. He completed his PhD at Princeton University in 1996 under Elias Stein and joined UCLA the same year, where he has been a full professor since 2000 and has held the James and Carol Collins Chair in Mathematics since 2007. In 2006 he received the Fields Medal, mathematics' highest honor, for contributions across several areas of analysis and combinatorics. In November 2023, after co-authoring a proof of the Polynomial Freiman-Ruzsa conjecture over finite fields with Tim Gowers, Ben Green and Freddie Manners, Tao led a rapid collaborative effort with Yael Dillies and Bhavik Mehta to formalize the entire proof in the Lean 4 proof assistant using a tool called Blueprint, completing the verification within weeks. He has continued to build public infrastructure for formalized mathematics, including a Lean companion to his own real analysis textbook and, in 2026, a registry called Palomar for tracking Lean verified proofs amid a rise in AI generated mathematical claims.
